# Future directions — almost-lossless compression beyond the pigeonhole bound

Derived from the formalised results in `Catalog/Logic/AlmostLossless/`
(`Core`, `Hashing`, `Scheme`, `Instances`, `ExactPlanar`, `Derandomisation`),
each conjecture below is falsifiable by a single counterexample or by a
machine-checkable proof.

---

## FD1 — The birthday penalty is unavoidable for pairwise-independent codebooks

**Conjecture.** Let `h : A → S → M` be a hash family that is *pairwise
independent* (`#{a | h a x = h a y} · |M| = |A|` for all `x ≠ y`, an equality,
not just the 2-universal inequality).  Then for every `T` with
`|T| ≤ sqrt(|M|)` the probability that a uniform seed is injective on `T`
satisfies
`P(injective on T) ≤ exp(-c · |T|² / |M|)` whenever the difference set of `T`
has `Ω(|T|²)` distinct projective directions.  Consequently no pairwise
independent family attains the information-theoretic alphabet size `|T|` of
`AlmostLossless.epsilon_pigeonhole_iff`; the square in
`AlmostLossless.exists_quadratic_rate_scanScheme` is necessary in this class.

**The key insight is** that the exact planar count
`AlmostLossless.exact_card_collides_planar` (`1 + d(p-1)` bad seeds for `d`
projective directions) turns "probability of a collision" into "measure of a
pencil of hyperplanes", so lower bounds on `d` — a purely projective-geometric
quantity — become lower bounds on the failure probability.

**Why now?** The planar case is already an equality, proved and cross-checked
numerically (Section 3 of `ComputationalEvidence.md`); the only missing
ingredient is the inclusion–exclusion over the subspace lattice in dimension
`k ≥ 3`, where the current data show the naive formula fails.

---

## FD2 — Exact failure probability in all dimensions via the subspace lattice

**Conjecture.** For the inner-product family over `(ZMod p)^k` and a typical set
`T` whose difference directions span the subspaces `V₁,…,V_d`, the number of bad
seeds equals `∑_{∅ ≠ I ⊆ [d]} (-1)^{|I|+1} p^{k - dim span{z_i : i ∈ I}}`, i.e.
the Möbius function of the lattice of subspaces generated by the directions
governs the exact failure probability.

**The key insight is** that `{a : ⟨a,z⟩ = 0}` is a hyperplane and the bad set is
a union of hyperplanes, so the exact count is a matroid/Möbius computation over
`𝔽_p`, not a probabilistic estimate: the union bound is precisely the first
Bonferroni term of this expansion.

**Why now?** `AlmostLossless.card_bad_seeds` already proves the `k = 2` instance
(pairwise intersections trivial ⇒ Möbius expansion truncates), and the failure of
the naive formula at `p = 13, k = 3` isolates exactly the missing higher-order
terms.

---

## FD3 — Constant-time decoding at optimal rate

**Conjecture.** There is an explicit scheme with codeword alphabet of size
`(1 + o(1))|T|` (matching `epsilon_pigeonhole_iff`, no squaring) whose decoder
performs `O(1)` expected candidate tests, obtained by composing a bucket hash of
range `|T|` with a *rate-optimal* index inside each bucket rather than a second
independent hash.

**The key insight is** that `AlmostLossless.avg_decodeCost_bucketed_le` is an
equality for pairwise independent families (`1 + (|T|-1)/m₁`, verified exactly in
Section 4 of `ComputationalEvidence.md`), so the bucket structure costs nothing
in *time*; the entire rate loss is in the checksum, which can be replaced by an
index of `⌈log₂(bucket size)⌉` bits.

**Why now?** All the moving parts — honest uniqueness decoding
(`honest_scanCode`), exact cost accounting (`ScanScheme.decodeCost_eq`) and the
exact `ε`-pigeonhole optimum — are formalised, so the conjecture reduces to
constructing the intra-bucket index and re-running the same failure analysis.

---

## FD4 — A finite Shannon source coding theorem in this framework

**Conjecture.** For an i.i.d. source of block length `n` with rational symbol
weights, the typical set `T_{n,δ} = {x : 2^{-n(H+δ)} ≤ μ(x) ≤ 2^{-n(H-δ)}}`
satisfies `μ.prob T_{n,δ} ≥ 1 - δ` for `n ≥ n₀(δ)` and `|T_{n,δ}| ≤ 2^{n(H+δ)}`;
combined with `AlmostLossless.exists_quadratic_rate_scanScheme` this yields an
*explicit, honest, never-silently-wrong* compressor of rate `2(H+δ)` bits per
symbol with an `O(|T|)`-time decoder, and combined with
`AlmostLossless.epsilon_pigeonhole_iff` a matching converse at rate `H-δ`.

**The key insight is** that every coding-theoretic ingredient of the source
coding theorem is already proved here in exact rational arithmetic; what remains
is purely a concentration statement about the source, so the theorem splits
cleanly into "information theory" (done) and "law of large numbers" (to do).

**Why now?** `epsilon_pigeonhole_iff` shows the *only* quantity that matters is
the size of a `(1-ε)`-probability set, so the whole of Shannon's theorem is
reduced to bounding `|T_{n,δ}|` — a single Chebyshev estimate.

---

## FD5 — Closing the additive gap in the rate/decoding-work trade-off

**Status of the two sides (both now theorems in `Complexity.lean`).**  Every
scan scheme with `m` codewords obeys `w ≥ max(1, t/m)` candidate tests per
typical word (`AlmostLossless.avg_decodeCost_ge`,
`AlmostLossless.one_le_decodeCost`), while a *pairwise independent* bucket hash
achieves exactly `w = 1 + (t-1)/m` on average over its seed
(`AlmostLossless.avg_decodeCost_bucketed_eq`).  The two differ by an additive
constant close to `1`.

**Conjecture.** The randomized value is optimal *among seeded schemes with no
preprocessing of `T`*: any scan scheme whose candidate sets are determined by a
2-universal hash satisfies `E_seed[w] ≥ 1 + (t-1)/m`, whereas *with*
preprocessing (a perfect hash, which exists by
`AlmostLossless.exists_perfect_seed` once `m > t(t-1)`) the value `w = 1` is
attainable.  Hence the exact cost of insisting on a fresh random seed rather
than a precomputed one is `(t-1)/m` tests — no more, no less.

**The key insight is** that `avg_decodeCost_bucketed_eq` turns the expected
work into a *pair-counting* quantity, so optimality among seeded schemes becomes
a statement about the collision count of a hash family, exactly the quantity
controlled by `sum_collisionCount_mul_le`.

**Why now?** Both endpoints are formalised and the numerics of Section 4 of
`ComputationalEvidence.md` sit on the conjectured value to the digit; the open
part is a lower bound over *all* 2-universal families, i.e. a converse to the
union bound rather than yet another application of it.

---

## Closed during this cycle

Two conjectures raised while writing this file were proved before the cycle
ended and are now theorems in `Catalog/Logic/AlmostLossless/Optimality.lean`:

* *Randomness never helps, for every source* —
  `AlmostLossless.randomized_epsilon_pigeonhole` and
  `AlmostLossless.exists_deterministic_code_of_ensemble`: an ensemble with
  average failure `≤ ε` implies a deterministic code with failure `≤ ε`.
* *Honesty is free* — `AlmostLossless.exists_scanScheme_of_code`: every code is
  matched on its correct set by a uniqueness-scan code that is honest by
  construction and whose decoder probes at most **one** candidate; the only
  price is one extra alphabet symbol.
